text:
sree: heads up — noticed shared-pool us-west-2 qlen spike ~15:03 UTC. p95 latency for small chat rose from ~0.9s to 1.8s. looks like a single tenant ramped ~5x. attaching logs in case thread needs them.
jonah: saw the same. culprit tenant=acme-ml-prod. their burst jobs spun up ~3k sessions in 2m. autoscaler didn’t add capacity because reserved capacity is pegged. infra-bot: [autoscaler] throttle_events=47, node_pressure=high
lena: can we soft-throttle upstream of the router? current admission control is node-scoped. propose a per-tenant token-bucket + early backpressure signal to client SDKs.
maya: +1 from product. we also need per-tenant queue-length visibility in Console (gauge + heatmap). ops teams are blind today.
dan: quick implementation idea: expose tenant_queue_size and tenant_backpressure_state in metrics-proxy as gauges. can roll to canary first.
jonah: also think about graceful fallbacks: when a tenant hits backpressure, route to model-compact (lower memory/latency) or reduce max_tokens. avoids user-visible errors.
sree: agreed. router should evaluate: if tenant_queue > threshold AND predicted_latency > X -> fallback to compatible smaller model and emit event for billing.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: initiating rollout "tenant-metrics-gauges" -> canary infra-canary-2
lena: for tests i'll run a synthetic noisy-tenant via loadgen. example command: ```loadgen --tenant acme-ml-prod --rps 2500 --seq 512 --duration 600``` will reproduce qlen growth quickly.
jonah: note: don't want hard eviction unless absolutely necessary. prefer soft-throttle (delay + 429-style response) and a clear owner-visible tag "soft-throttled" in Console so SREs/SEs can triage.
maya: also adding cost context — reducing bursts should cut ephemeral GPU spin-up cost. i'll work with finance to estimate monthly savings for the exec deck.
dan: i'll run a simulator patch (admission_control.proto add burst_credit field) and run a 2-hour sim across tenants to validate fairness metrics (P99 latency, throughput, eviction rate).
infra-bot: experiment scheduled: tenant-fairness-sim v3 at 2025-03-14T15:30Z (will post artifacts here)
sree: rollout plan proposal: (1) metrics + Console signal to canary (48h), (2) token-bucket soft-throttle in router + canary (24h), (3) fallback routing to model-compact (canary), (4) measure perf + cost 48h, (5) full rollout. volunteers?
jonah: i'll own router fallback (3). will canary in us-west-2 after metrics are live. also will wire event for audit log and billing hook.
lena: i'll own metrics + test harness (1). will add alerts: tenant_queue > 100 for 10m -> page SRE and notify tenant owner. need help with thresholds.
maya: i'll coordinate cost model with finance and owner comms for paid customers.
dan: i'll run sims and post results. will also check impact on region fallback (if us-west-2 saturates, prefer routing lower-priority requests to us-east-1 if latency budget allows).
jonah: follow-up question — should we provide an API for tenants to request transient burst credits (paid)? makes sense for enterprise customers who need occasional spikes.
sree: yes but gate it: API + billing + strict limits. prefer soft-throttle by default and an opt-in paid burst override that still respects capacity.
ops-bot: noted: created JIRA EPIC RED-INFRA-1258 "tenant soft-throttle + metrics"; added checklist and initial owners. :calendar:
jonah: ok, sync tomorrow 14:00 UTC to triage thresholds and canary timing. I'll post a short spec before then.
lu: (minor) remember to include network egress pressure in the sim — some failures were network-related last quarter and looked like GPU pressure.
sree: good call, include network and KV cache eviction behavior in the sim matrix. thanks everyone.
